# Results -- Study 258 (Baker-Wurgler) on the real S&P 500 tape

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). Recipe: read the
month-end Baker-Wurgler sentiment level at the end of month t (a published,
lagged figure) and predict the ^GSPC return earned during month t+1 (one-month
execution lag). Sort next-month returns by prior-sentiment tertile, regress
next-month return on lagged sentiment (Newey-West HAC), and stress a tradable
long-when-fearful timing overlay against unconditional buy-and-hold.
**Price-only** ^GSPC returns (no dividends) -- labeled on the Signal axis.
The sentiment index is a hardcoded **reconstruction** of the BW regime structure.
As-of **2026-06-17**.*

## Data stamp

| Source | Window | Shape | Fingerprint |
|--------|--------|-------|-------------|
| ^GSPC monthly close (repo cache, price-only) | 1965-02 -> 2026-06 | 737 return-months | `24206d518a4c` (ret) |
| BW sentiment reconstruction (hardcoded annual -> monthly) | 1965-01 -> 2025-12 | 732 months | `d88ba1009823` (sent) |
| ^RUT size proxy (small-minus-large leg) | 1987-10 -> 2026-06 | 465 months | -- |

## Primary specification (next-month S&P return by prior sentiment tertile)

| Regime (prior sentiment) | Next-month return | Vol (ann) | HAC *t* | n |
|--------------------------|-------------------|-----------|---------|---|
| **Low** (most fearful) | **+8.78%/yr** | 15.8% | +2.36 | 246 |
| Mid | +9.24%/yr | 13.4% | +3.41 | 245 |
| **High** (most greedy) | **+7.16%/yr** | 15.8% | +2.22 | 246 |
| **Low - High spread** | **+0.81%/yr** | -- | **+0.32** | 492 |

- The **sign is correct** (Baker-Wurgler contrarian): low-sentiment months
  (+8.78%/yr) beat high-sentiment months (+7.16%/yr).
- But the **low-minus-high spread is +0.81%/yr at HAC *t* = +0.32** -- statistically
  indistinguishable from luck.
- **Predictive regression** of next-month return on lagged sentiment:
  slope = **-31.0 bps per sentiment unit**, HAC *t* = **-1.29**, R² = 0.0025.
  The slope is negative (the right, contrarian sign) but **does not clear |t| >= 2**.

## Block-bootstrap CI on the low-minus-high spread Sharpe

| Statistic | Value |
|-----------|-------|
| Spread Sharpe 95% CI | **[-0.257, +0.356]** |
| Fraction of resamples negative | 38.5% |

The CI **straddles zero** -- there is no robust spread.

## Sub-period analysis -- decay and sign flip

| Period | Regression HAC *t* | Low-regime | High-regime | n |
|--------|--------------------|-----------|-------------|---|
| 1965-1989 | **-1.39** | +9.1%/yr | +0.7%/yr | 299 |
| 1990-2007 | -0.49 | +14.0%/yr | +9.9%/yr | 216 |
| 2008-2026 | -0.16 | +7.3%/yr | **+14.1%/yr** | 222 |

The contrarian tilt was strongest in **1965-1989** (the original BW sample era) and
has decayed since. By **2008-2026 the sign flips**: high-sentiment months (+14.1%/yr)
actually *beat* low-sentiment months (+7.3%/yr) -- classic post-publication decay.

## Cross-sectional leg -- small-minus-large (^RUT - ^GSPC, 1987-2026)

| Regime | SMB next-month | 
|--------|----------------|
| Low sentiment | +1.66%/yr |
| High sentiment | -1.83%/yr |
| SMB regression slope | -17.3 bps/unit, HAC *t* = -0.77 (n=465) |

BW says speculative/small names suffer *most* after high sentiment. The proxy sign is
right (small beats large after fear, lags after greed) but is **insignificant** (|t| < 1).

## Tradability -- timing overlay vs buy-and-hold

Rule: be long the market in low-sentiment months, flat otherwise; 5 bps one-way x NAV.

| Strategy | Return | Sharpe (ann) | Max DD |
|----------|--------|--------------|--------|
| Long-when-fearful (net) | +2.9%/yr | +0.32 | -45.8% |
| **Unconditional buy-and-hold** | **+8.39%/yr** | **+0.56** | -52.6% |
| Short-the-greedy variant (net) | +0.5%/yr | +0.04 | -64.4% |

Switches: ~0.73/yr (low turnover, 220 bps total cost over 60 years). The timing rule
**loses to buy-and-hold** on both return and Sharpe -- sitting out greedy months sits
out too much of the equity risk premium. Shorting the high-sentiment months is worse.

## Positive control -- the engine finds a contrarian effect when planted

On the deterministic synthetic tape (`data.synthetic_market`):

| Planted contrarian_bps | Regression slope | HAC *t* |
|------------------------|------------------|---------|
| 0 (null) | +4.7 bps/unit | +0.23 |
| 60 | -52.4 bps/unit | **-2.58** |

The engine reads a clean, significant negative (contrarian) slope when one exists, and
~zero on the null. The real tape simply does not carry a comparable signal at the index level.

## Verdict

- **Signal -- WEAK.** The Baker-Wurgler contrarian *sign* is right on the aggregate
  index (low-sentiment months beat high), and the literature (BW 2006, 2007) is strong,
  but the predictive slope HAC *t* = -1.29 and the low-minus-high spread *t* = +0.32
  **never clear the |t| >= 2 bar** on the real tape. The bootstrap Sharpe CI straddles
  zero, the effect is concentrated in 1965-1989, and the sign flips post-2008.
  Right idea, no robust significance -> **WEAK** (literature support keeps it off None).
- **Tradability -- MIRAGE.** A long-when-fearful timing overlay underperforms
  buy-and-hold (+2.9%/yr net vs +8.39%/yr) at a lower Sharpe; the short variant is worse.
  There is no tradable edge on the aggregate index beyond passive buy-and-hold.
- **Price-only / reconstruction -- named.** ^GSPC returns are price-only (no dividends);
  the cross-regime spread is roughly dividend-neutral. The sentiment index is a hardcoded
  reconstruction of the BW regime structure, not the verbatim NYU file.
